newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Maystadt to tackle abuse of savings books.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Maystadt to tackle abuse of savings books.

text.p: Belgian Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt plans to tackle the abuse of tax exemption on interest income from savings books, he told financial daily L'Echo in an interview on Friday.

"It is normal that tax authorities try to make sure that the law is respected. Which is clearly not the case, as the number of tax-exempt savings books amounts to nearly 20 million, about twice as many as the number of Belgians. Therefore, I think there must be abuse," he said.

Interest income from savings books -- the most popular savings instrument in Belgium -- is exempt from taxes up to 55,000 francs ($1,540) per year, but many Belgians simply open two or more accounts at several banks.
As the 15 percent withholding tax is not deducted at source, investors can walk away with untaxed interest income well above the 55,000 franc threshold.

L'Echo said the Belgian Banking Association had proposed to the finance ministry to make investors pay the withholding tax at source, which they would be able to reclaim in their tax returns later. The paper quoted Maystadt as saying the proposal would be investigated.
